correctness.rationale: For vertex-transitive nonempty simple graphs the complete pair witness spectrum Σ={(e(u,v),{(e(u,w),e(v,w)):w≠u,v}):u≠v} is exactly the information needed for a three-round EF game: the first vertex is matched by transitivity, the second by a matching pair type, and the third by an available atomic witness or repeated vertex. For products of d≥2 cycles, degree 2d and at most two common neighbors imply private neighbors, and an absent 00 pair pattern only in small excluded size cases; the C3×C3 exception was separately checked. Common neighbors of adjacent pairs identify 3-cycle factors, and distance-two versus distance≥3 pairs classify nonadjacent pair types. The product diameter sum floor(n_i/2) gives exactly four multi-factor spectra. Single-cycle direct analysis gives four short exceptions and stabilized C_n,n≥7; eight distinct classes result. Independent full pair-witness enumeration on 16 representatives across d=1..4 corroborated all eight classes and found C7≡3 C4×C4; proof handles arbitrary d and n_i. Family-relative maximum smallest representative is 27 vertices at C3×C3×C3.

originality.rationale: Brown–Hoshino gives the bare-cycle rank-three cutoff 7, and general FO game pair-characterization is standard. The result adds the classification for all d and factor lengths, including nontrivial equivalences C7≡3 high-dimensional all-n_i≥4 products and the exact mixed-triangle strata. Verbitsky surveys graph EF methods without this torus-specific eight-spectrum theorem. Relevant Resultary toroidal graph results concerned topological invariants, not FO rank-three theories.
